title: Sequence Clustering
text: silhouette plot shows well sequence fits assigned cluster. Values near 1 indicate good fit; values near 0 suggest sequence clusters; negative values indicate possible misclassification. MDS (multidimensional scaling) plot projects distance matrix 2D, showing cluster separation.
code: plot(clust, type = "silhouette") plot(clust, type = "mds")

title: Sequence Clustering
text: distance metric defines (dis)similarity sequences measured. words, quantifies different two sequences . Nestimate currently supports 9 distance metrics comparing sequences: Different metrics may produce different clustering results. need choose based research question: Hamming: compares sequences position position (best aligned sequences equal length). Edit distances (lv, osa, dl): allow insertions deletions (best sequences may shifted vary length). LCS: captures shared subsequences (best overall patterns matter exact alignment). can specify distance metric want use dissimilarity argument: distance metrics may take additional arguments. example, Hamming distance accepts temporal weighting emphasize earlier later positions:
code: # Levenshtein distance (allows insertions/deletions) clust_lv <- build_clusters(net, k = 3, dissimilarity = "lv") clust_lv$silhouette #> [1] 0.2689417  # Longest common subsequence clust_lcs <- build_clusters(net, k = 3, dissimilarity = "lcs") clust_lcs$silhouette #> [1] 0.1836091 # Emphasize earlier positions (higher lambda = faster decay) clust_weighted <- build_clusters(net,                                 k = 3,                                dissimilarity = "hamming",                                weighted = TRUE,                                lambda = 0.5) clust_weighted$silhouette #> [1] 0.2337931

title: Sequence Clustering
text: default, Nestimate uses PAM (Partitioning Around Medoids) form clusters, assigns sequence cluster represented central sequence (medoid). Besides PAM, Nestimate supports hierarchical clustering methods, build clusters step step progressively merging similar units tree-like structure (dendrogram): ward.D2 (“Ward’s Method, Squared Distances”): Minimizes increase within-cluster variance using squared distances. Typically produces compact, well-separated clusters. ward.D (“Ward’s Method”): alternative implementation Ward’s approach using different distance formulation. Similar behavior, results may vary slightly. complete (“Complete Linkage”): Defines distance clusters maximum distance members. Produces tight, compact clusters. average (“Average Linkage”): Uses average distance pairs points across clusters. Provides balance compactness flexibility. single (“Single Linkage”): Uses minimum distance points two clusters. Can capture chain-like structures may lead - loosely connected clusters. mcquitty (“McQuitty’s Method” / “WPGMA”): weighted version average linkage gives equal weight clusters regardless size. centroid (“Centroid Linkage”): Defines cluster distance based distance cluster centroids (means). Can produce intuitive groupings may introduce inconsistencies hierarchy. use methods instead PAM, need provide method argument build_clusters.
code: # Ward's method (minimizes within-cluster variance) clust_ward <- build_clusters(net, k = 3, method = "ward.D2") clust_ward$silhouette #> [1] 0.5694224  # Complete linkage clust_complete <- build_clusters(net, k = 3, method = "complete") clust_complete$silhouette #> [1] 0.8019662

title: Sequence Clustering
text: Instead clustering sequences based similar one another, can cluster together based transition dynamics. Mixture Markov models (MMM) fit separate Markov models, sequences assigned cluster whose transition structure best matches observed behavior. implement MMM, can use build_mmm(), returns net_mmm object full model details: net_mmm object contains posterior probabilities, model fit statistics (BIC, AIC, ICL), per-cluster transition matrices $models. cluster_diagnostics() works , MMM-specific columns (mixing share, average posterior probability, per-cluster classification error): posterior plot type shows distribution sequence’s max posterior probability, faceted cluster. Tight distributions near 1 indicate clean assignment; spread-distributions indicate fuzzy clusters.
code: mmm_fit <- build_mmm(net, k = 2) summary(mmm_fit) #> Mixed Markov Model #>   Sequences: 526  |  Clusters: 2  |  States: 3 #>   ICs: LL = -10074.921  |  BIC = 20256.351  |  AIC = 20183.841  |  ICL = 20536.530 #>   Quality: AvePP = 0.782  |  Entropy = 0.642  |  Class.Err = 0.0% #>  #>   Cluster  N            Mix%   AvePP #>   1        334 (63.5%)  55.7%  0.766 #>   2        192 (36.5%)  44.3%  0.808 #>  #> --- Cluster 1 (55.7%, n=334) --- #>               Directive Evaluative Metacognitive #> Directive         0.647      0.144         0.208 #> Evaluative        0.549      0.269         0.181 #> Metacognitive     0.429      0.257         0.314 #>  #> --- Cluster 2 (44.3%, n=192) --- #>               Directive Evaluative Metacognitive #> Directive         0.565      0.301         0.134 #> Evaluative        0.447      0.462         0.090 #> Metacognitive     0.398      0.435         0.166 #>   component     prior n_assigned mean_posterior     avepp #> 1         1 0.5566955        334      0.7663911 0.7663911 #> 2         2 0.4433045        192      0.8080450 0.8080450 diag_mmm <- cluster_diagnostics(mmm_fit) diag_mmm #> Cluster Diagnostics (mmm) [k = 2] #>   Sequences: 526  |  Clusters: 2  |  States: 3 #>   Quality: AvePP = 0.782  |  Entropy = 0.642  |  Class.Err = 0.0% #>   ICs: LL = -10074.921  |  BIC = 20256.351  |  AIC = 20183.841  |  ICL = 20536.530 #>  #>   Cluster  N            Mix%   AvePP  Class.Err% #>   1        334 (63.5%)  55.7%  0.766   0.0% #>   2        192 (36.5%)  44.3%  0.808   0.0% plot(diag_mmm, type = "posterior")

title: Sequence Clustering
text: sequences grouped, goal usually compare transitions behave within group. single transition network estimated sequences averages across groups hides contrast. Estimating one network per cluster preserves group’s distinct dynamics — nodes, different edge weights. result netobject_group: list netobjects sharing node set, one per cluster. Every group network supports downstream operations single netobject — plotting via plot(), resampling via bootstrap_network(), group-level edge comparison via permutation(). Two paths produce netobject_group: Manual — fit clustering build_clusters() cluster_mmm(), pass fitted clustering build_network(). Shortcut — cluster_network() collapses fitting network materialization one call either distance MMM clustering. Distance clustering groups sessions sequence similarity. Model-based MMM clustering groups Markov model best explains sequence’s transitions.

title: Network Estimation and Visualization with Nestimate + cograph
text: Nestimate unified network estimation package R. provides single entry point — build_network() — accepts sequence data, wide-format behavioral data, numeric matrices estimates networks using 10 built-methods. result netobject inherits cograph_network, every object produced Nestimate can plotted splot() directly. core design principle estimation visualization separate concerns: Nestimate handles computation (network construction, bootstrapping, permutation testing, clustering, multi-cluster analysis), cograph handles rendering. separation means analyst writes estimation code gets publication-ready figures without adapter code manual class conversion. Beyond single-network estimation, Nestimate provides complete statistical toolkit: Bootstrap stability analysis (bootstrap_network) — identifies edges survive resampling sampling artifacts. Permutation-based group comparison (permutation) — tests whether edges differ significantly conditions. Multi-cluster multi-level analysis (csum, summarize_clusters) — aggregates node-level networks cluster-level summaries hierarchical visualization. Centrality stability (centrality_stability) — assesses whether centrality rankings robust case dropping. Group-level operations — bootstrapping, permutation testing, plotting work grouped networks additional code. tutorial walks full pipeline group_regulation_long dataset shipped Nestimate.

what: Is First-Order Enough? Multi-Order Model Selection
title: Higher-Order Network Analysis with Simplicial Complexes
text: investing higher-order analysis, answer: sequential memory actually matter? Multi-Order Generative Model (MOGen; Scholtes 2017) fits Markov models increasing orders compares using information criteria. Higher-order models fit better exponentially parameters — AIC BIC find best tradeoff.  plot traces AIC BIC functions Markov order. higher-order models always fit better terms raw log-likelihood (parameter space contains lower-order one), meaningful comparison fit complexity. AIC penalises parameter 2; BIC penalises log(n), dataset much larger 2 — BIC favors small orders much aggressively AIC. Order 0: Actions independent — sequential structure. Order 1: standard Markov model sufficient. Order 2+: Higher-order dependencies exist. first-order TNA miss . Even order 1 globally optimal (BIC), specific pathways may still exhibit higher-order behavior — global model averages states. HON analysis detects local patterns. next section adds complementary, principled hypothesis test often reveals signal BIC parsimonious flag. mogen_transitions() extracts transitions given order, showing two-step contexts lead different outcomes: row second-order pathway. column two-state context, predicted next state, count empirical frequency, probability conditional P(| ). high count combined high probability predictive context: knowing previous two states pins next one. high count low probability common ambiguous context — frequent data, successor distribution spread . plot_simplicial() accepts mogen_transitions() data.frame directly. takes top pathways count renders smooth blob shared circular layout, path’s intermediate states blue target state red. Repeated states (like Specify -> Command -> Specify) get distinct positions blob covers three visually distinct nodes rather collapsing line.  zoom single frequent pathway, set max_pathways = 1 let data.frame drive selection. mogen_transitions() returns rows already sorted count, max_pathways = N always picks top N:  MOGen uses information criteria. complementary, principled approach permutation-exact LRT markov_order_test(): order kk, tests H0H_0: “process order (k−1)(k-1)” H1H_1: “process order kk” reframing conditional-independence test (k+1)(k+1)-grams. null distribution built shuffling successor labels within context — test exact H0H_0, plug-MLE bias sparse (k+1)(k+1)-gram tables.  output reveals tension hidden single criterion. BIC selects smallest order (heavy parsimony penalty). AIC permutation LRT flag higher orders significantly better — every increase order yields G2G^2 statistic far tail within-context permutation null. right panel makes concrete: grey density null G2G^2 distribution per order, colored vertical line observed value. line sits right tail, H0H_0 rejected higher order carries genuine information beyond previous one. takeaway: sequential memory exists dataset. BIC penalises parameter space order 3 enormous (4,706 degrees freedom order-3 test alone), data pay cost. Order-selection answers global question. Transition entropy answers per-state question: predictable state’s next move? transition_entropy() computes Shannon row-entropy H(P[, ]) = -sum_j P[,j] log P[,j] every state, chain-level entropy rate h(P) = sum_i pi_i H(P[, ]) (Shannon-McMillan-Breiman per-step uncertainty stationary distribution pi), redundancy H(pi) - h(P) (much previous state reduces uncertainty next).  bar state’s outgoing-distribution entropy bits; bar’s width proportional stationary probability, visual area sums entropy rate h(P). dashed red line marks h(P); dotted line marks ceiling log_2(n) every state uniform outgoing distribution. States whose bar pokes near ceiling unpredictable hubs (next state essentially random); short bars deterministic — arrive , next step largely fixed.

Components merge one another β0\beta_0 falls; new loops appear (β1\beta_1 jumps ) later get filled triangles (β1\beta_1 falls ). shape curves fingerprint network’s topology — smooth monotone β0\beta_0 curve means graph well-connected every scale, long flat plateau sudden drops marks discrete merging events. Persistence diagram (right): point one topological feature, plotted (birth threshold, death threshold). Points hug diagonal birth death close — short-lived features, almost certainly noise. Points far diagonal lived wide range thresholds robust topological signal. Color encodes dimension; size encodes persistence (death − birth) persistent features pop visually.

what: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Unified network estimation, analysis, validation behavioral, psychological, panel data. Nestimate comprehensive R package estimating, validating, comparing networks behavioral sequence data, psychological scales, longitudinal panel data. single entry point — build_network() — dispatches 14 built-estimators. Every network type shares validation pipeline: bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation testing, split-half reliability, centrality stability.

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Network Estimation & Visualization Higher-Order & Simplicial Complexes Model Assessment Permutation Tests Nested Data Comparing Networks

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Transition Networks Sequence Plots & Comparison Clustering & Multi-Level Analysis Markov Stability Sequence Pattern Comparison

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
code: # From CRAN install.packages("Nestimate")  # Development version devtools::install_github("mohsaqr/Nestimate")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: dynamic network methods use build_network(). Pass event log action, actor, time columns — preprocessing needed.

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
code: library(Nestimate) data(human_long)  net <- build_network(human_long, method = "tna",                      action = "action", actor = "session_id", time = "time")  # Per-group networks in one call group_nets <- build_network(human_long, method = "tna",                             action = "action", actor = "session_id",                             time = "time", group = "phase")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: wtna() builds networks binary (one-hot) data using temporal windows — directed transitions windows, undirected co-occurrence within windows, mixed network combining .
code: data(learning_activities) net_wtna  <- wtna(learning_activities, actor = "student",                   method = "transition", type = "relative") net_mixed <- wtna(learning_activities, actor = "student",                   method = "both", type = "relative")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: cooccurrence() builds undirected co-occurrence networks 6 input formats (delimited fields, long/bipartite, binary matrix, wide sequence, lists) 8 similarity methods (Jaccard, cosine, association strength, Dice, ).
code: # From a long-format data frame net_co <- cooccurrence(human_long, field = "action", by = "session_id",                        similarity = "jaccard", threshold = 0.1)

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: implemented scratch dependency igraph, qgraph, bootnet.
code: data(srl_strategies) net_gl  <- build_network(srl_strategies, method = "glasso") net_mgm <- build_network(mixed_data, method = "mgm")   # scales + demographics  predictability(net_gl)   # R-squared per node from network structure

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_mlvar() estimates three networks simultaneously ESM/EMA diary data — three pillars mlVAR analysis single function call: Temporal (directed) — lagged fixed effects: predicts across time Contemporaneous (undirected) — partial correlations within-person residuals: moves together right now -subjects (undirected) — partial correlations person means: differs Machine-precision equivalence mlVAR::mlVAR() validated across 25 real ESM datasets, runs 1.45× faster.
code: data(chatgpt_srl) fit <- build_mlvar(chatgpt_srl, vars = c("planning", "monitoring", "evaluation"),                    id = "id", day = "day", beep = "beep")  fit$temporal          # directed network of lagged effects fit$contemporaneous   # undirected within-person partial correlations fit$between           # undirected between-persons partial correlations coefs(fit)            # tidy data.frame: beta, SE, t, p, CI for every edge

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_gimme() estimates separate network person using Group Iterative Mean Estimation (GIMME) algorithm, aggregates group-level picture. Use -person heterogeneity matters single group network average meaningfully different individuals.
code: fit_g <- build_gimme(panel_data, vars = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), id = "id") fit_g$group_network       # aggregated group-level paths fit_g$individual_networks # one network per person

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_clusters() partitions sequences k groups using pairwise distance matrices. Supports 9 distance metrics 8 clustering algorithms. build_clusters() build_mmm() results pass directly build_network().
code: clust <- build_clusters(net, k = 3, dissimilarity = "hamming", method = "ward.D2") plot(clust, type = "silhouette") cluster_nets <- build_network(clust, method = "tna")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_mmm() discovers latent subgroups sequences share similar transition dynamics via EM — without pre-labelling groups. BIC/AIC/ICL model selection via compare_mmm().
code: mmm   <- build_mmm(net, k = 3) compare_mmm(net, k = 2:6)   # model selection plot + table mmm_nets <- build_network(mmm, method = "tna")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_mcml() decomposes network macro (-cluster) micro (within-cluster) layers nodes belong known groups.
code: clusters <- list(Metacognitive = c("Planning", "Monitoring"),                  Cognitive     = c("Elaboration", "Organisation")) mcml <- cluster_summary(net, clusters) mcml$macro$weights

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Capture dependencies beyond first-order transitions:
code: hon  <- build_hon(net, max_order = 2) pathways(hon)                      # arrow-notation path strings hypa <- build_hypa(net) hypa$over                          # over-represented paths with p-values

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Go beyond edges — find cliques, holes, high-order connectivity using tools algebraic topology.
code: sc <- build_simplicial(net, method = "clique") betti_numbers(sc)          # connected components, cycles, voids euler_characteristic(sc) ph <- persistent_homology(net)  # track topology across thresholds plot(ph) qa <- q_analysis(sc)       # Atkin's Q-connectivity structure vectors

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Visualize raw sequence data index plots state distribution charts — clustering.
code: # Sequence index plot: one row per person, coloured by state sequence_plot(net)  # After clustering: faceted by cluster clust <- build_clusters(net, k = 3) sequence_plot(clust, type = "index")  # State distribution over time distribution_plot(net, type = "area") distribution_plot(clust, type = "bar")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: sequence_compare() extracts k-gram patterns grouped sequences, counts per-group frequencies, tests statistical differences via permutation — answering question “groups actually behave differently, ?”
code: data(human_long) net <- build_network(human_long, method = "tna",                      action = "action", actor = "session_id",                      time = "time", group = "phase")  res <- sequence_compare(net, sub = 2:4, test = "chisq", adjust = "fdr") res$patterns                        # per-pattern frequencies + p-values plot(res)                           # back-to-back pyramid chart plot(res, style = "heatmap")        # heatmap for many patterns

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: association_rules() mines “B” patterns sequences binary matrices using Apriori algorithm. Returns support, confidence, lift, conviction every rule threshold.
code: rules <- association_rules(net, min_support = 0.05, min_confidence = 0.6) rules$rules                       # tidy data.frame, sorted by lift pathways(rules)                   # rules as arrow-notation strings  # From a raw binary matrix rules2 <- association_rules(binary_mat, min_support = 0.1)

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: predict_links() scores unobserved node pairs using structural similarity, identifying missing connections likely exist. evaluate_links() computes AUC, precision, recall held-edges.
code: preds <- predict_links(net)       # common neighbours, Adamic-Adar, Katz, ... head(preds$scores)                # sorted by predicted score  # Evaluate against known missing edges eval  <- evaluate_links(net, held_out = test_edges) eval$auc

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: markov_stability() measures stable network partition random-walk dynamics different time scales — resolution-free way find communities. passage_time() computes expected first-passage return times states.
code: stab <- markov_stability(net, times = seq(0.1, 10, 0.1)) plot(stab)                # stability vs time-scale curve  pt <- passage_time(net) pt$first_passage          # expected steps to reach state j from state i pt$return_time            # expected steps to return to the same state

title: Discover Association Rules from Sequential or Transaction Data — association_rules
text: Uses level-wise Apriori (Agrawal & Srikant, 1994) full pruning step: join step generates k-candidates, (k-1)-subsets verified frequent support counting. critical efficiency k >= 4.

title: Discover Association Rules from Sequential or Transaction Data — association_rules
text: support P(B). Fraction transactions containing antecedent consequent. confidence P(B | ). Fraction antecedent transactions also contain consequent. lift P(B) / (P() * P(B)). Values > 1 indicate positive association; < 1 indicate negative association. conviction (1 - P(B)) / (1 - confidence). Measures departure independence. Higher = stronger implication.

Jeffreys prior posterior transitions state \(\) \(\mathrm{Dirichlet}(c_i + \alpha)\), \(c_i\) observed outgoing counts. edge probability marginally Beta-distributed, posterior mean difference two networks available closed form credible interval obtained Monte Carlo. complement permutation: permutation test answers "difference extreme chance?"; Bayesian comparison answers "plausible range true difference, precisely estimated given counts?". edge outgoing transitions source state yields wide credible interval even row-normalised probability looks decisive. bayes_compare() also accepts two net_edge_betweenness objects (source method "relative" ). Edge betweenness nonlinear function whole transition matrix, instead Beta marginals full transition matrix drawn group's row-wise Dirichlet posterior edge betweenness recomputed every draw - Bayesian analogue permutation()'s edge-betweenness dispatch. result summarises posterior EB(x) - EB(y): diff posterior mean difference, prob_x/prob_y hold posterior mean betweenness matrices, observed_diff plug-difference two input networks. inputs must use invert setting.

Ordinal items. cor_method = "polychoric" (requires lavaan package) estimates node-level within-cluster networks polychoric correlations - appropriate Likert items. Within-cluster networks follow within: "reestimate" (default) re-fits estimator member columns alone - honest conditional structure subsystem; "subnetwork" slices node-level weight matrix descriptive (pcor/glasso retains conditioning --cluster nodes). code: set.seed(1) n <- 200 sigma <- matrix(0.15, 6, 6) sigma[1:3, 1:3] <- 0.5 sigma[4:6, 4:6] <- 0.5 diag(sigma) <- 1 z <- matrix(rnorm(n * 6), n, 6) %*% chol(sigma) df <- as.data.frame(z) names(df) <- c("a1", "a2", "a3", "b1", "b2", "b3") clusters <- list(A = c("a1", "a2", "a3"), B = c("b1", "b2", "b3"))  fit <- build_mcml_pc(df, clusters, aggregation = "composite",                      method = "cor") fit            # macro (cluster-level) weights #> MCML for Psychometric Networks (experimental) #>   Aggregation: composite | Estimator: cor | Within: reestimate | cor: pearson | Weights: equal #>   6 nodes in 2 clusters (A: 3, B: 3) #>  #> Macro weights: #>       A     B #> A 0.000 0.235 #> B 0.235 0.000 summary(fit)   # one row per macro edge #>   from to   weight #> 1    A  B 0.235001 plot(fit)      # heatmap of the same weights

text: Estimation delegated idiographic::fit_mlvar() (clean-room home temporal idiographic estimators), called estimator = "lmer", temporal = "fixed", contemporaneous = "fixed". pipeline follows mlVAR's lmer path exactly: Drop rows NA id/day/beep optionally grand-mean standardize variable. Expand per-(id, day) beep grid right-join original values, producing augmented panel (augData). Add within-person lagged predictors (L1_*) person-mean predictors (PM_*). outcome variable fit lmer(y ~ within + -except--PM + (1 | id)) REML = FALSE. Collect fixed-effect temporal matrix B, -effect matrix Gamma, random-intercept SDs (mu_SD), lmer residual SDs. Contemporaneous network: cor2pcor(D %*% cov2cor(cor(resid)) %*% D). -subjects network: cor2pcor(pseudoinverse(forcePositive(D (- Gamma)))). Validated machine precision (max_diff < 1e-10) mlVAR::mlVAR() 25 real ESM datasets openesm 20 simulated configurations, exact equality (max_diff == 0) pre-delegation Nestimate implementation layers, coefficients, observation counts across lag/standardize/day/beep configurations. data carry -person variance (random-intercept SD zero), -subjects network estimable. title: Build a Multilevel Vector Autoregression (mlVAR) network — build_mlvar
code: # A three-variable ESM panel: 20 people x 20 beeps. `tired` is driven by # `happy` one beep earlier, so the temporal network should recover it. if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   n_beep <- 20   ar1 <- function(n, phi) as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(n), phi,                                                    method = "recursive"))   panel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(i) {     happy <- ar1(n_beep, 0.4)     data.frame(       id    = i,       beep  = seq_len(n_beep),       happy = happy + stats::rnorm(1),       calm  = ar1(n_beep, 0.3) + stats::rnorm(1),       tired = 0.5 * c(0, happy[-n_beep]) + stats::rnorm(n_beep) +               stats::rnorm(1)     )   }))   fit <- build_mlvar(panel, vars = c("happy", "calm", "tired"),                      id = "id", beep = "beep")   fit   coefs(fit)   summary(fit) } #>           network n_nodes n_edges density mean_abs_weight n_positive n_negative #> 1        temporal       3       6       1      0.11569402          2          4 #> 2 contemporaneous       3       3       1      0.05304465          1          2 #> 3         between       3       3       1      0.15389239          2          1

title: Build a Simplicial Complex — build_simplicial
text: Constructs simplicial complex network higher-order pathway object. Two construction methods available: Clique complex ("clique"): every clique thresholded non-zero graph becomes simplex. Edges absolute weight \(\geq\) threshold retained. standard bridge graph theory algebraic topology. Pathway complex ("pathway"): higher-order pathway net_hon net_hypa becomes simplex. type = "vr" (alias "rips"), input treated non-negative distance / dissimilarity matrix Vietoris-Rips filtration constructed: k-simplex \(\sigma\) enters \(\max_{(,j) \\sigma} d(,j)\). Use max_scale cap filtration diameter; edges d(,j) > max_scale excluded. Filtration values attached $filtration returned object persistent_homology() can read directly.

title: Cluster Summary Statistics — cluster_summary
text: x Network input. Accepts multiple formats: matrix Numeric adjacency/weight matrix. Row column names used node labels. Values represent edge weights (e.g., transition counts, co-occurrence frequencies, probabilities). netobject network object built build_network. weight matrix x$weights aggregated; bare cograph_network coerced netobject first. tna tna object tna package. Extracts x$weights. mcml mcml object returned unchanged. clusters Cluster/group assignments nodes. Accepts multiple formats: NULL (default) usable : clusters required NULL raises error. Auto-detection cluster column netobject's node table happens build_mcml, calls function detected assignment. vector Cluster membership node, order matrix rows/columns. Can numeric (1, 2, 3) character ("", "B"). Cluster names derived unique values. Example: c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3) assigns first two nodes cluster 1. data.frame data frame first column contains node names second column contains group/cluster names. Example: data.frame(node = c("", "B", "C"), group = c("G1", "G1", "G2")) named list Explicit mapping cluster names node labels. List names become cluster names, values character vectors node labels must match matrix row/column names. Example: list(Alpha = c("", "B"), Beta = c("C", "D")) method Aggregation method combining edge weights within/clusters. Controls multiple node--node edges summarized: "sum" (default) Sum edge weights. Best count data (e.g., transition frequencies). Preserves total flow. "mean" Average edge weight. Best cluster sizes differ want control size. Note: input already transition matrix (rows sum 1), "mean" avoids size bias. Example: cluster 5 nodes 5x weight cluster 1 node. "median" Median edge weight. Robust outliers. "max" Maximum edge weight. Captures strongest connection. "min" Minimum edge weight. Captures weakest connection. "density" Sum (non-zero) edge weights divided number possible edges two clusters (n_i * n_j). Normalizes cluster size combinations. zero/NA edges stripped aggregation, equals "mean" exactly cluster-pair block fully dense (zero edges), strictly smaller "mean" zero edges present (divides larger possible-edge count). "geomean" Geometric mean positive weights. Useful multiplicative processes. directed Logical. TRUE (default), treat network directed. ->B B->separate edges. FALSE, edges undirected matrix symmetrized processing. compute_within Logical. TRUE (default), compute within-cluster transition matrices cluster. cluster gets n_i x n_i matrix showing internal node--node transitions. Set FALSE skip computation better performance -cluster summary needed.

cluster-level (macro) weights #> MCML Network #> ============ #> Type: aggregate  | Method: sum  #> Nodes: 10  | Clusters: 3  #>  #> Clusters: #>   1 (3): A, B, C #>   2 (3): D, E, F #>   3 (4): G, H, I, J #>  #> Macro (cluster-level) weights: #>        1      2      3 #> 1 4.0786 5.6031 5.6788 #> 2 4.4388 3.9691 6.6812 #> 3 6.7692 5.8665 8.6995 summary(cs)   # one row per cluster #>   cluster size within_total between_out between_in #> 1       1    3     4.078562    11.28182   11.20801 #> 2       2    3     3.969112    11.12004   11.46957 #> 3       3    4     8.699460    12.63571   12.35999  # ----------------------------------------------------- # Named list clusters (more readable) # ----------------------------------------------------- clusters <- list(   Alpha = c("A", "B", "C"),   Beta = c("D", "E", "F"),   Gamma = c("G", "H", "I", "J") ) cluster_summary(mat, clusters) #> MCML Network #> ============ #> Type: aggregate  | Method: sum  #> Nodes: 10  | Clusters: 3  #>  #> Clusters: #>   Alpha (3): A, B, C #>   Beta (3): D, E, F #>   Gamma (4): G, H, I, J #>  #> Macro (cluster-level) weights: #>        Alpha   Beta  Gamma #> Alpha 4.0786 5.6031 5.6788 #> Beta  4.4388 3.9691 6.6812 #> Gamma 6.7692 5.8665 8.6995  # ----------------------------------------------------- # A netobject as input: its weight matrix is aggregated # ----------------------------------------------------- seqs <- data.frame(   T1 = c("A", "C", "B", "D"), T2 = c("B", "D", "A", "C"),   T3 = c("C", "A", "D", "B") ) net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative") cluster_summary(net, list(G1 = c("A", "B"), G2 = c("C", "D"))) #> MCML Network #> ============ #> Type: aggregate  | Method: sum  #> Nodes: 4  | Clusters: 2  #>  #> Clusters: #>   G1 (2): A, B #>   G2 (2): C, D #>  #> Macro (cluster-level) weights: #>    G1 G2 #> G1  1  1 #> G2  1  1  # ----------------------------------------------------- # Different aggregation methods # ----------------------------------------------------- summary(cluster_summary(mat, clusters, method = "sum"))   # total flow #>   cluster size within_total between_out between_in #> 1   Alpha    3     4.078562    11.28182   11.20801 #> 2    Beta    3     3.969112    11.12004   11.46957 #> 3   Gamma    4     8.699460    12.63571   12.35999 summary(cluster_summary(mat, clusters, method = "mean"))  # average #>   cluster size within_total between_out between_in #> 1   Alpha    3     4.078562    1.095792   1.057301 #> 2    Beta    3     3.969112    1.049971   1.111438 #> 3   Gamma    4     8.699460    1.052976   1.029999 summary(cluster_summary(mat, clusters, method = "max"))   # strongest #>   cluster size within_total between_out between_in #> 1   Alpha    3     4.078562    1.774085   1.900114 #> 2    Beta    3     3.969112    1.800406   1.655449 #> 3   Gamma    4     8.699460    1.786146   1.805074  # ----------------------------------------------------- # Skip within-cluster computation for speed # ----------------------------------------------------- cluster_summary(mat, clusters, compute_within = FALSE) #> MCML Network #> ============ #> Type: aggregate  | Method: sum  #> Nodes: 10  | Clusters: 3  #>  #> Clusters: #>   Alpha (3): A, B, C #>   Beta (3): D, E, F #>   Gamma (4): G, H, I, J #>  #> Macro (cluster-level) weights: #>        Alpha   Beta  Gamma #> Alpha 4.0786 5.6031 5.6788 #> Beta  4.4388 3.9691 6.6812 #> Gamma 6.7692 5.8665 8.6995  # code: # A three-variable ESM panel: 20 people x 20 beeps. `tired` is driven by # `happy` one beep earlier, so the temporal network should recover it. if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   n_beep <- 20   ar1 <- function(n, phi) as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(n), phi,                                                    method = "recursive"))   panel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(i) {     happy <- ar1(n_beep, 0.4)     data.frame(       id    = i,       beep  = seq_len(n_beep),       happy = happy + stats::rnorm(1),       calm  = ar1(n_beep, 0.3) + stats::rnorm(1),       tired = 0.5 * c(0, happy[-n_beep]) + stats::rnorm(n_beep) +               stats::rnorm(1)     )   }))   fit <- build_mlvar(panel, vars = c("happy", "calm", "tired"),                      id = "id", beep = "beep")   fit   coefs(fit)   summary(fit) } #>           network n_nodes n_edges density mean_abs_weight n_positive n_negative #> 1        temporal       3       6       1      0.11569402          2          4 #> 2 contemporaneous       3       3       1      0.05304465          1          2 #> 3         between       3       3       1      0.15389239          2          1

text: x netobject, cograph_network, numeric square matrix, netobject_group whose members j compared. print() plot() methods: object class net_comparison. ... Ignored. plot.net_comparison() print.net_comparison(): Ignored. y netobject, cograph_network, numeric square matrix. scaling Scaling applied weight matrices comparison. One : "none" Identity (default). "minmax" \((w - \min) / (\max - \min)\); maps \([0, 1]\). "max" \(w / \max(|w|)\); preserves sign. "rank" Min-max average ranks; ordinal scaling. "zscore" \((w - \bar w) / s_w\); standard score. "robust" \((w - \mathrm{med}(w)) / \mathrm{mad}(w)\); Huber-style robust z-score, resists outliers. "log" \(\log(w)\); requires \(w > 0\). "log1p" \(\log(1 + w)\); admits \(w \ge 0\). "softmax" Numerically stable softmax flattened vector. "quantile" Empirical CDF flattened vector. "frobenius" Divide matrix Frobenius norm \(\|W\|_F = \sqrt{\sum w_{ij}^2}\); matrix-level normalisation. "row" Row-stochastic normalisation (row's absolute values sum 1). meaningful non-negative matrices; rows summing zero left unchanged. Scalings produce negative weights (zscore, robust) compatible network = TRUE side--side metrics use Nestimate's base-R Floyd-Warshall, handles negative weights. measures Character vector centrality measures compare. Empty default (centrality block). built-measure valid: "OutStrength", "InStrength", "ClosenessIn", "ClosenessOut", "Closeness", "Betweenness", "BetweennessRSP", "Diffusion", "Clustering", "InCloseness", "OutCloseness". Unknown names ignored warning. network Logical. Include side--side network metrics summary()? Default TRUE. , j netobject_group: index name two member networks compare. Defaults 1L 2L. type Character. One "scatter" (default - edge-weight scatter OLS fit correlation overlay), "heatmap" (n n grid x - y differences using diverging palette), "diff_hist" (histogram |x - y| absolute differences rug + density), "weight_dist" (overlaid distributions |x| |y| edge weights), "" (2 2 grid four panels; requires gridExtra package). combined type = "" combined = TRUE (default), four panels stitched 2x2 gtable. FALSE, returns named list four ggplots can printed, saved, re-laid-independently. Ignored type values.

title: Compare two or more networks — compare_networks
text: Guarding. Ratios never Inf/NaN: ratio NA weight_b == 0, rel_diff NA weights 0, log_ratio = log1p() - log1p(b) NA either weight negative. pseudo-counts added. Cells. Every cell weight matrix row, including diagonal edges absent one network (weight 0); networks undirected <= cells kept. Inference. "permutation" (via permutation()) adds perm_effect, perm_p, perm_sig edges nodes, two rows M (sum absolute edge differences) S (largest absolute edge difference) global permutation p-values; actor, reassignment moves whole actors global also gains rows ICC, Design effect (edges) Design effect (M). "bayes" (via bayes_compare()) adds bayes_diff (posterior mean difference), bayes_ci_lower, bayes_ci_upper, bayes_pd (probability direction), bayes_p, bayes_sig edges; rope, bayes_p_rope (normal approximation posterior mean SD) bayes_decision. "bootstrap" (via vertex_compare()) appends structural rows (density, mean weight, centralization, reciprocity) global boot_se, boot_ci_lower, boot_ci_upper, boot_z, boot_p, boot_sig. Unified sig evidence columns take permutation result run (edges nodes), else Bayesian one (edges – Bayesian backend edge-level). Permutation Bayesian tests need networks carry data (build_network() output, tna objects, rebuilt); plain matrices support "bootstrap" .

text: One colour contract every view every backend: "#4A6FE3" marks network_a (reference, one set) higher two, "#D33F6A" marks network_b, grey marks difference; plotted quantity always diff = - b. Colour never carries sign alone – solid line circular marker repeat "higher", dashed line square marker repeat "b higher", printed value carries sign. test run, evidence shown opacity starred (edge node views) annotated (inference view) label: non-significant difference faded, never deleted.

title: Build a Co-occurrence Network — cooccurrence
text: data Input data. Accepts: data.frame delimited column (field + sep). data.frame long/bipartite format (field + ). binary (0/1) data.frame matrix (auto-detected). wide sequence data.frame matrix (non-binary). list character vectors (element transaction). field Character. entity column - determines nodes . delimited format, single column whose values split sep. long/bipartite format, item column. multi-column delimited, vector column names whose split values pooled per row. Character NULL. links nodes. long/bipartite format, grouping column (e.g., "paper_id", "session_id"). unique value defines one transaction. NULL (default), entities co-occur within row/document. sep Character NULL. Separator splitting delimited fields (e.g., ";", ","). Default NULL. similarity Character. Similarity measure applied raw co-occurrence counts. One : "none" Raw co-occurrence counts. "jaccard" \(C_{ij} / (f_i + f_j - C_{ij})\). "cosine" \(C_{ij} / \sqrt{f_i \cdot f_j}\) (Salton's cosine). "inclusion" \(C_{ij} / \min(f_i, f_j)\) (Simpson coefficient). "association" \(C_{ij} / (f_i \cdot f_j)\) (association strength / probabilistic affinity index; van Eck & Waltman, 2009). "dice" \(2 C_{ij} / (f_i + f_j)\). "equivalence" \(C_{ij}^2 / (f_i \cdot f_j)\) (Salton's cosine squared). "relative" Row-normalized: row sums 1. threshold Numeric. Minimum edge weight retain. Edges value set zero. Applied similarity normalization. Default 0. min_occur Integer. Minimum entity frequency (number transactions entity must appear ). Entities threshold dropped computing co-occurrence. Default 1 (keep ). diagonal Logical. TRUE (default), diagonal co-occurrence matrix kept (item self-co-occurrence = item frequency). FALSE, diagonal zeroed. top_n Integer NULL. specified, return top top_n edges weight. Default NULL (edges). ... Currently unused.

title: Build a Co-occurrence Network — cooccurrence
text: Six input formats supported, auto-detected combination field, , sep: Delimited: field + sep (single column). cell split sep, trimmed, de-duplicated per row. Multi-column delimited: field (vector) + sep. Values multiple columns split, pooled, de-duplicated per row. Long bipartite: field + . Groups ; unique values field within group form transaction. Binary matrix: field//sep, values 0/1. Columns items, rows transactions. Wide sequence: field//sep, non-binary. Unique values across row form transaction. List: plain list character vectors. pipeline converts formats list character vectors (transactions), optionally filters min_occur, builds binary transaction matrix, computes crossprod(B) raw co-occurrence counts, normalizes via chosen similarity, applies threshold top_n filtering.

title: Transition Entropy Network — entropy_network
text: x netobject, cograph_network, tna object, row-stochastic numeric transition matrix, wide sequence data.frame (rows = actors, columns = time-steps; relative transition network built automatically). base Numeric. Logarithm base. 2 (default) bits, exp(1) nats, 10 hartleys. weight Character. Edge weight definition: "contribution" (default) \(\pi_i P_{ij} \log_b(1/P_{ij})\) - edge's additive share entropy rate; edge weights sum exactly \(h(P)\). Thick edges transitions frequent unpredictable. "surprisal" \(\log_b(1/P_{ij})\) - information content observing transition, ignoring often occurs. Thick edges rare, surprising transitions. Low surprisal = expected transition; edge-level predictability reading. "production" \(F_{ij} \log_b(F_{ij}/F_{ji})\) \(F_{ij} = \pi_i P_{ij}\) - edge's contribution entropy production rate (irreversibility). Positive dominant direction pair, negative reverse; two always sum \((F_{ij}-F_{ji}) \log_b(F_{ij}/F_{ji}) \ge 0\). Pairs flow one direction infinite production excluded (weight 0); count reported $params$n_oneway_pairs. Total included pairs $params$production_rate - 0 iff chain reversible (detailed balance). scaling Character. "none" (default) keeps weights base-units. "share" (contribution ) expresses edge percentage entropy rate - weights sum 100 label reads "transition holds x% process's unpredictability"; comparable across networks regardless state count base. "chance" (surprisal ) divides \(\log_b n\) - surprisal chance-level transition \(n\) next states equally likely: 1 = chance level, 1 = expected transition, 1 = rarer chance. normalize Logical. TRUE (default), rows sum 1 normalised automatically (warning).

title: Cut an Event Log into Pathways — extract_pathways
text: data long-format data.frame, one row per event, already chronological order within group (order supplied). action Name column holding state / event label. group Character vector column names defining unit pathway may cross – typically actor, actor session. order Optional column giving within-group event order. NULL (default) existing row order used. type cut make: "unit" (default) one pathway per group. terminal, group truncated last terminal state pathway ends outcome rather whatever followed. "segments" consecutive, non-overlapping pathways: group cut every terminal state, pathway ends one. Every event belongs exactly one pathway. "anchored" one pathway per occurrence anchor, closing next terminal state. Pathways may overlap events terminal next anchor belong none. anchor State opens pathway type = "anchored". Ignored cuts. Default NULL. terminal States close pathway, closing state included. Required "segments" "anchored"; optional "unit", truncates. resolve Optional named list giving resolution label append pathway's final state. element character vector states; pathway takes label first element whose states occur , order list specific least. Pathways matching nothing labelled "Unresolved". label becomes last element path value closes, raw final state kept ends. sep Separator used pasting path. Default " -> ".

title: Cut an Event Log into Pathways — extract_pathways
text: data.frame one row per pathway: group columns, pathway (integer id within group), path (states pasted sep), length, opens (first state) closes (last state). resolve, closes holds resolution label instead ends column carries raw final state. Pathways returned order occur.

Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
text: Computes one eigenvector-style centralities net_hypergraph: clique-motif (CEC), Z-eigenvector (ZEC), H-eigenvector (HEC). variant captures influence differently - CEC flattens group structure via clique expansion, ZEC HEC propagate higher-order groups directly.

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
code: hypergraph_centrality(   hg,   type = "clique",   max_iter = 1000L,   tol = 1e-08,   normalize = TRUE )

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
text: hg net_hypergraph (build_hypergraph() bipartite_groups()). type Character vector, subset c("clique", "Z", "H"). Default "clique". "Z" "H" need uniform hypergraph (every hyperedge two members size). max_iter Maximum number power-iteration steps "Z" "H" iterations. Default 1000. "clique" solved directly. tol Convergence tolerance L1 change successive iterates "Z" "H". Default 1e-8. iteration reach within max_iter steps warns class nestimate_no_converge. normalize Logical. TRUE (default), returned centrality vector L2-normalized unit norm (compatible igraph::eigen_centrality()'s scale type "clique"). FALSE, vector rescaled largest absolute entry 1.

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
text: named list, one component per requested type, order given type. component numeric vector length hg$n_nodes named hg$nodes. hypergraph hyperedges yields -zero vectors. Requesting "Z" "H" non-uniform hypergraph raises error class nestimate_nonuniform_hypergraph.

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
text:
Clique-motif eigenvector centrality (CEC): forms clique-expanded pairwise graph \(W\) \(W_{ij} = |\{e : , j \e\}|\) returns leading eigenvector \(W\). Equivalent running igraph::eigen_centrality() clique_expansion() output. vector solved directly symmetric eigendecomposition connected component (Perron-Frobenius makes leading eigenvalue connected component simple), power iteration, oscillates clique expansion bipartite (example star pairs). several components share largest eigenvalue, result projection uniform vector onto joint leading eigenspace; components smaller leading eigenvalue score zero. Z-eigenvector centrality (ZEC): solves eigen-equation hyperedge tensor, $$\lambda\, x_i \;=\; \sum_{e 
i }\; \prod_{j \e,\; j 
eq } x_j,$$ shifted power iteration. Tensor products normalization evaluated log space retain finite, normalized centralities large hyperedges. H-eigenvector centrality (HEC): solves $$\lambda\, x_i^{k-1} \;=\; \sum_{e 
i }\; \prod_{j \e,\; j 
eq } x_j.$$ Uniform hypergraphs . Benson (2019) defines ZEC HEC \(k\)-uniform hypergraphs. mixed sizes right-hand side mixes polynomial degrees, equation scale-free solution: vector satisfies normalisation chosen inside iteration. Hyperedges one member contribute nothing ignored uniformity check. mixed sizes use "clique", keep one size build_hypergraph() (include_pairwise = FALSE).

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
text: "clique" (CEC) variant validated igraph::eigen_centrality (cosine ~ 1). "Z" "H" variants (experimental) - validated clean-room list-based tensor power iteration (operator, different loop structure); R package exposes tensor eigenvectors primitive independent comparison.

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
text: Benson, . R. (2019). Three hypergraph eigenvector centralities. SIAM Journal Mathematics Data Science 1(2), 293-312. arXiv:1807.09644.

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hypergraph_centrality
code: df <- data.frame(   player  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "D", "C", "D", "E"),   session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S3", "S3") ) hg <- bipartite_groups(df, "player", "session") hypergraph_centrality(hg) #> $clique #>         A         B         C         D         E  #> 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.2672612 0.2672612  #>   # Z and H need a uniform hypergraph: here every session has three players df3 <- data.frame(   player  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "D", "C", "D", "E"),   session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S3") ) hypergraph_centrality(bipartite_groups(df3, "player", "session"),                       type = c("clique", "Z", "H")) #> $clique #>         A         B         C         D         E  #> 0.5127870 0.5127870 0.4559848 0.4559848 0.2413603  #>  #> $Z #>         A         B         C         D         E  #> 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.4364358 0.4364358 0.2182179  #>  #> $H #>         A         B         C         D         E  #> 0.4867656 0.4867656 0.4556438 0.4556438 0.3330103  #>

Diagonal zero. Hyperedge-level (length n_hyperedges m x m)  edge_sizes Hyperedge sizes \(|e|\). edge_pairwise_overlap m x m matrix: |e_i intersect e_j|. Global (scalars)  density k-uniform hypergraphs: m / choose(n, k). mixed sizes: sum(|e|) / (n * m) (mean fraction nodes per hyperedge). avg_edge_size Mean edge_sizes. size_distribution Tabulation hyperedge sizes (passed hg). intersection_profile Distribution pairwise hyperedge intersection sizes - useful spotting whether hyperedges overlap mostly trivially share substantial cores (et al. 2020). pairwise_participation Fraction node pairs co-appearing least one hyperedge. n_nodes, n_hyperedges Convenience scalars. print.hypergraph_measures(): input x invisibly.

title: Structural measures for a hypergraph — hypergraph_measures
text: measures computed via standard matrix operations binary incidence \(B = (b_{ij})\) \(b_{ij} = 1\) iff node \(\) hyperedge \(j\): hyperdegree = rowSums(B), edge_sizes = colSums(B) co_degree = tcrossprod(B) (zero diagonal) edge_pairwise_overlap = crossprod(B) (zero diagonal) overlap_coefficient[, j] = overlap[, j] / min(edge_sizes[], edge_sizes[j]) jaccard[, j] = overlap[, j] / (edge_sizes[] + edge_sizes[j] - overlap[, j]) Empty hypergraph (n_hyperedges == 0) returns trivial zeros empty matrices.

what: Test the Markov order of a sequential process — markov_order_test
title: Test the Markov order of a sequential process — markov_order_test
text: Principled test whether categorical sequence best described \(k\)-th order Markov chain. order \(k = 1, \ldots,\) max_order, function computes classical likelihood-ratio statistic (\(G^2\)) conditional independence \(s \perp x \mid w\), \(w\) \((k-1)\)-gram context, \(x\) extra (k-th-back) state added order \(k\), \(s\) next state. \(H_0\) (order-\((k-1)\) correct), \(s\) independent \(x\) given \(w\). null distribution obtained within-\(w\) (conditional) permutation test: context \(w\) successor labels exchangeable \(H_0\), shuffling \(s\) within \(w\)-group keeps every count null hypothesis conditions . windows sequence overlap, approximates reference distribution \(G^2\) rather giving exactly (exact test sample whole sequences counts; Besag & Mondal, 2013). plug-MLE bias refitting per replicate. asymptotic \(\chi^2\) p-value reported alongside reference. Order selection sequential: order raised test rejects, stops first non-rejection. reported optimal_order therefore highest \(k\) whose test - every test - rejected level alpha, .e. one first non-rejection; 0 order 1 already rejected, max_order test accepts.

text: Uses Kemeny-Snell fundamental matrix formula: $$M_{ij} = \frac{Z_{jj} - Z_{ij}}{\pi_j}, \quad       Z = (- P + \Pi)^{-1}$$ \(\Pi_{ij} = \pi_j\). Requires ergodic (irreducible, aperiodic) chain.

title: Persistence Landscape — persistence_landscape
text: Computes persistence landscape (Bubenik 2015) persistence diagram. (birth, death) pair contributes tent function $$\Lambda_{(b,d)}(t) = \max(0, \min(t - b, d - t)).$$ \(k\)-th landscape function \(\lambda^{(k)}(t)\) \(k\)-th largest \(\{\Lambda_{(b_i,d_i)}(t)\}_i\) \(t\). Landscapes stable bottleneck distance form Banach-space embedding persistence diagrams. Essential classes excluded: tent function undefined infinitely-lived class finite grid, pairs death = Inf (VR mode) pairs death = 0 birth > 0 (clique-mode encoding essential class) dropped landscape built. finite pair remains requested dimension, every landscape function zero grid.

title: Persistent Homology — persistent_homology
text: Computes persistent homology via full boundary-matrix reduction \(\mathbb{Z}/2\) (Edelsbrunner, Letscher & Zomorodian 2000). returned persistence diagram pairs k-dimensional homology class simplex whose addition creates (birth) simplex whose addition destroys (death). Essential classes - never killed - reported death = 0 clique mode (similarity scale, descending) death = Inf VR mode (distance scale, ascending). Two filtration modes supported: type = "clique" Weighted clique filtration. Input treated similarity matrix; high-weight simplices appear early. k-simplex \(\sigma\), filtration value \(\min_{(,j) \\sigma}\,|w(,j)|\). Thresholds run high low. type = "vr" Vietoris-Rips filtration non-negative distance matrix. k-simplex \(\sigma\), filtration value \(\max_{(,j) \\sigma}\,d(,j)\). Thresholds run low high. Use max_scale cap filtration diameter.

text: Standardized residuals always computed 2xG contingency table (pattern vs. everything else) using textbook formula (o - e) / sqrt(e * (1 - r/N) * (1 - c/N)). describe much group's count given pattern deviates expectation independence, scaled approximately N(0,1) null. optional test argument chooses inference method: "permutation" Shuffles group labels across sequences recomputes per-pattern statistic (row-wise Euclidean residual norm). Answers: "pattern's distribution associated group membership actor level?" Respects sequence unit analysis; can underpowered number sequences small. "chisq" Runs chisq.test 2xG table per pattern. Answers: "group streams generate pattern different rates?" Treats k-gram occurrence event; fast powerful even sequences, iid assumption makes optimistic sequences strongly autocorrelated. "none" Skip inference. residuals, frequencies, proportions returned. P-values adjusted across patterns (per-pattern) using method supported p.adjust. default "fdr" (Benjamini-Hochberg).

text: replicate draws n vertex indices replacement sets W_b[, j] = W[idx_i, idx_j]. original vertex drawn two different positions, -diagonal cell structural self-pair; following Snijders & Borgatti, cells filled weight randomly chosen pair distinct original vertices. Diagonal entries carry original self-weight resampled vertex (W[idx_i, idx_i]) - self-loops meaningful transition networks never altered. undirected networks substitution applied symmetrically replicates stay symmetric. Built-statistics (computed -diagonal part weight matrix): density Proportion non-zero -diagonal cells. mean_weight Mean non-zero -diagonal weights. centralization Freeman-type strength centralization: sum(max(s) - s) / ((n - 1) * max(s)) s total node strength absolute weights. 0 nodes equal strength, approaching 1 star. reciprocity Directed networks . title: Window-based Transition Network Analysis — wtna
text: Transitions: Uses crossprod(X[-n,], X[-1,]) count often state active time t state j time t+1. Co-occurrence: Uses crossprod(X) count states simultaneously active row. Within-cluster networks re-estimated default (within = "reestimate") since pcor submatrix subsystem’s pcor network. Item diagnostics $loadings: signed loadings (reverse-keyed items detected via leading eigenvector within-block matrix flipped composites), cross-cluster strengths, misfit flag item connected another cluster (warned). Composites tolerate missing data (row-wise renormalized weighted means); Composite item weights selectable via weighting — ten built-schemes spanning three views cluster: scale scored ("equal", "item_total"), network’s view ("strength", "eigen", "closeness", "betweenness", "expected_influence", "specificity" — misfit margin weighting, zeroing items belong much another cluster), latent-variable view ("pca", "factor"); plus fully custom weighting via named numeric vector function(W_block, data_block, nodes). aggregation = "loadings" alias composite + strength. "factor" weighting exposes extraction method via fa_method: "ml" (factanal), "paf" (iterated principal axis), "minres" (ULS), "cfa" (one-factor lavaan model; cor_method = "polychoric" categorical DWLS factor model) — operating cor_method-consistent correlation structure. Reverse-keyed handling works every sign-carrying scheme (item-total correlations computed eigen-sign-pre-oriented columns reversed member contaminate small clusters). cor_method = "polychoric" (via lavaan) supports ordinal items; id_col drops identifier columns convert_sequence_format(format = "frequency") actor-profiles feed function directly (within-person co-occurrence view event data).
